## Figuring out probability of success from data

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column}

Suppose we go looking for kāhuli

![image credit: DOFAW](img/intro-like/kahuli.jpg){width="50%"}
::::

:::: {.column}

And out of 8 visits we find them 2 times

```{r}
kahuli <- c(0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0)
kahuli
```

This is a binomial situation with 8 trials, but what is $p$?

::::

:::



## Figuring out probability of success from data

This is a binomial situation with 8 trials, but what is $p$?

```{r}
kahuli
```

Let's ask ourselves: what's the probability of these data given different values of $p$? For example, $\mathbb{P}(n = 2 \mid N = 8, p = 0.9)$:

```{r}
p <- 0.9
dbinom(2, size = 8, prob = p)
```



## Figuring out probability of success from data

This is a binomial situation with 8 trials, but what is $p$?

```{r}
kahuli
```

Find the value of $p$ for which $\mathbb{P}(n = 2 \mid N = 8, p)$ is *highest*, that is a good guess for the value of $p$ 


## Figuring out probability of success from data

Find the value of $p$ for which $\mathbb{P}(n = 2 \mid N = 8, p)$ is *highest*, that is a good guess for the value of $p$ 

```{r}
pp <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.05)

l <- dbinom(2, size = 8, prob = pp)
l
```


## Figuring out probability of success from data

Find the value of $p$ for which $\mathbb{P}(n = 2 \mid N = 8, p)$ is *highest*, that is a good guess for the value of $p$ 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center

lik_fun <- data.frame(pp, l)

gp_lik <- ggplot(lik_fun, aes(pp, l)) +
    geom_point(size = 6) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 2) +
    xlab("p") +
    ylab("P(n = 2 | N = 8, p)") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 20), 
          axis.title = element_text(size = 22, face = "italic"))

gp_lik
```

## Figuring out probability of success from data

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width=70%}

$\mathbb{P}(n = 2 \mid N = 8, p)$ is *highest* when $p = 0.25$

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center


gp_lik +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.25, color = "red", linewidth = 2)


```

::::

:::: {.column width=30%}

Interesting! 

We learned probability is also *frequency*

The frequency of successes was $\frac{2}{8} = 0.25$

::::

:::


## Figuring out probability of success from data

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width=70%}

$\mathbb{P}(n = 2 \mid N = 8, p)$ is *highest* when $p = 0.25$

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center


gp_lik +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.25, color = "red", linewidth = 2)


```

::::

:::: {.column width=30%}

So we figured out a fancy way of finding $p = \frac{2}{8} = 0.25$

But this matters because *frequency* in more complex data will not be so clear cut

::::

:::

## Figuring out probability of success from data

What we figured out is in fact the *likelihood function*

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width=70%}

$\mathbb{P}(\text{data} \mid \text{parameters})$

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center


gp_lik +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.25, color = "red", linewidth = 2)


```

::::

:::: {.column width=30%}

And that maximizing it gives us a good estimate of the parameters

::::

:::


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence

Let's return to the simulated presence/absence data

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{P}(\text{presence}) &\sim Binom(N = 1, ~p) \\
p &= \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(-2 + 0.001 \times (\text{elevation}))}}
\end{aligned}
$$

```{r}
set.seed(123)
nobs <- 50
elev <- runif(nobs, 0, 5000)
p <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(-2 + 0.001 * elev)))
y <- rbinom(nobs, size = 1, prob = p)
dat <- data.frame(elev, y)
```


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence

Let's return to the simulated presence/absence data

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width=70%}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center

gp_pa <- ggplot(dat, aes(elev, y)) +
    geom_point(size = 6, alpha = 0.5) +
    xlab("Simulated elevation") + 
    ylab("Simulated\npresence/absence") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 20), 
          axis.title = element_text(size = 24))

gp_pa + 
    geom_function(fun = \(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-(-2 + 0.001 * x))), 
                  linewidth = 2) +
    annotate(geom = "text", x = 1900, y = 0.4, 
             label = expression(p == frac(1 , (1 + exp(-(a[0] + a[1] * elev))))), 
             hjust = "left", size = 8)
```

::::

:::: {.column width=30%}

Can we use MLE to find the values of $\hat{a_0}$ and $\hat{a_1}$ and will they close to the true values of $a_0 = -2$ and $a_1 = 0.001$?

::::

:::


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence



Can we use MLE to find the values of $\hat{a_0}$ and $\hat{a_1}$?

We need `dbinom`. But what should `size` be and `prob` be?


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


Can we use MLE to find the values of $\hat{a_0}$ and $\hat{a_1}$?

We need `dbinom`. But what should `size` be and `prob` be?


$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{P}(y \mid N = 1, ~p = f(x)) = ~&\mathbb{P}(y_1 \mid N = 1, ~p_1 = f(x_1)) \times \\
&\mathbb{P}(y_2 \mid N = 1, ~p_2 = f(x_2)) \times \cdots \times \\
&\mathbb{P}(y_n \mid N = 1, ~p_n = f(x_n)) \\
= ~&\prod_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i))
\end{aligned}
$$


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


Can we use MLE to find the values of $\hat{a_0}$ and $\hat{a_1}$?

We need `dbinom`. But what should `size` be and `prob` be?


$$
\mathbb{P}(y \mid N = 1, ~p = f(x)) = \prod_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i))
$$

```{r}
try_a0 <- -1 # close-ish to the truth
try_a1 <- 0.005
l <- dbinom(y, size = 1, 
            prob = 1 / (1 + exp(-(try_a0 + try_a1 * elev)))) |> 
    prod()
```


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


$$
\mathbb{P}(y \mid N = 1, ~p = f(x)) = \prod_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i))
$$

Sweet! What is the value of the likelihood function?

. . .

```{r}
l
```

. . .

...oh no



## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


$$
\mathbb{P}(y \mid N = 1, ~p = f(x)) = \prod_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i))
$$

***The issue:*** multiplying many numbers less than 1 $\Rightarrow$ very small number that our computer can't deal with.

Not to worry! ***Math to the rescue!***

## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


$$
\mathbb{P}(y \mid N = 1, ~p = f(x)) = \prod_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i))
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \log (\mathbb{P}(y &\mid N = 1, ~p = f(x)) ) \\
&= \log \left(\prod_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i)) \right) \\
&= \sum_{i = 1}^n\log \left(\mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i)) \right)
\end{aligned}
$$


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


$$
\begin{aligned}
\log (\mathbb{P}(y &\mid N = 1, ~p = f(x)) ) \\
&= \sum_{i = 1}^n\log \left(\mathbb{P}(y_i \mid N = 1, ~p_i = f(x_i)) \right)
\end{aligned}
$$


Logging both sides turns multiplication into addition 


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


Logging both sides turns multiplication into addition ***and doesn't change our parameter estimates***



```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center

gp_loglik <- ggplot(lik_fun, aes(pp, log(l))) +
    geom_point(size = 6) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 2) +
    xlab("p") +
    ylab("log(P(n = 2 | N = 8, p))") +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 20), 
          axis.title = element_text(size = 22, face = "italic")) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.25, color = "red", linewidth = 2)

gp_lik <- gp_lik +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.25, color = "red", linewidth = 2)

plot_grid(gp_lik, gp_loglik)

```

## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence


So we always work with the ***log likelihood function***



```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center

gp_loglik

```

## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence

Now we return to find the values of $\hat{a_0}$ and $\hat{a_1}$


```{r}
try_a0 <- -1 # close-ish to the truth
try_a1 <- 0.005

# log likelihood now
ll <- dbinom(y, size = 1, 
            prob = 1 / (1 + exp(-(try_a0 + try_a1 * elev))), 
            log = TRUE) |> 
    sum()

ll
```

That is a number we can work with!


## Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE): presence/absence

Looking over a range of $\hat{a_0}$ and $\hat{a_1}$ values we see a maximum!

::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width=70%}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-align: center


try_a <- expand.grid(a0 = seq(-8, 1, length.out = 40), 
                     a1 = seq(0.0001, 0.007, length.out = 40))


ll <- sapply(1:nrow(try_a), function(i) {
    dbinom(y, size = 1, 
            prob = 1 / (1 + exp(-(try_a$a0[i] + try_a$a1[i] * elev))), 
            log = TRUE) |> 
    sum()
})

ll <- data.frame(try_a, loglik = ll)



ggplot(ll, aes(a0, a1, z = loglik)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = loglik)) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c() +
    geom_contour(color = "black") +
    xlab(expression(hat(a[0]))) +
    ylab(expression(hat(a[1]))) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = FALSE) +
    geom_point(data = ll[which.max(ll$loglik), ], 
               mapping = aes(a0, a1), 
               shape = 4, size = 2, stroke = 2) +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 20), 
          axis.title = element_text(size = 22))
```

::::

:::: {.column width=30%}

And our estimates

$\hat{a_0}$ = `r ll[which.max(ll$loglik), "a0"]` <br>
$\hat{a_1}$ = `r ll[which.max(ll$loglik), "a1"]`

Are close to the true values

$a_0 = -2$  <br>
$a_1 = 0.001$

::::

:::
